---
title: "Results"
---

The 2,491 participants were mean age 76 y, 43% males and 57% females. The six clinical status groups, defined by [in-study phenotyping at two examinations and by dementia surveillance for up to 13.4 years (@suppfig-timeline)]{.rev}, included a stable normal group with no subsequent report of dementia (n = 1,581), a baseline prevalent dementia group (n = 161), and four prospective transition groups: baseline normal to mild cognitive impairment with no subsequent report of dementia (normal2mci, n = 99), stable MCI with no subsequent report of dementia (stable_mci, n = 49), normal to incident dementia (normal2incid, n = 494), and MCI to incident dementia (mci2incid, n = 107) (@tbl-dementia-category). Of the 255 participants who received an MCI diagnosis, 38.8% transitioned from normal cognition to MCI, 19.2% remained stable from baseline to end-of-follow-up, and 42.0% transitioned from baseline MCI to dementia. [Age, education and the three cognitive composite scores (memory, processing speed and working memory) differed across the six groups (each *P* < 0.001; @tbl-baseline). Compared with the stable normal group, every other group was older on average (mean 76.8–80.6 vs 74.4 years), more often had primary education only (23%–47% vs 18%), and had lower mean scores on all three cognitive composites. Among the four prospective transition groups, cognitive scores were lowest in the two with MCI at baseline (stable_mci and mci2incid), and the prevalent dementia group scored lowest of all.]{.rev}

### Stages exhibit distinct methylation patterns

We quantified the [covariate-adjusted effect size (ΔM, the difference in mean M-value)]{.rev} of the association between each CpG site and each transition stage or the prevalent dementia group relative to the [stable normal (reference) group (@supptbl-exemplar shows the full model output for one example CpG site)]{.rev}. There were 403 significant CpG sites (*P* < 1.0 × 10^−8^). Of these 403, there were 5 DMPs in the normal2mci, 62 in the stable_mci, 1 in the normal2incid transition, 9 in the mci2incid transition, and 326 in the prevalent dementia groups respectively (@suppdata-DMP403). These CpG sites were distributed across the whole genome, many of which are associated with genes that are critical for neurologic function (@suppfig-manhattan). [These genes included *NOTCH3*, whose mutations cause an inherited small-vessel disease with stroke and dementia [@RN45]; *BACE2*, which cleaves the amyloid precursor protein [@RN46]; *RAB7A*, part of the autophagy–lysosomal pathway that clears proteins in neurons [@RN48]; and *GLP1R*, which regulates insulin secretion and body weight [@RN85; @RN91] and encodes the target of semaglutide, recently tested in two phase 3 trials in early Alzheimer's disease [@RN84].]{.rev}

We then investigated the pairwise directionality and correlations of the DMP effect size between dementia groups, controlling for covariates. We found strong positive effect size correlations between prevalent dementia and the prospective dementia transition groups normal2incid (*r* = 0.87, [*P* = 3.12 × 10^−126^]{.rev}) and mci2incid (*r* = 0.86, [*P* = 3.87 × 10^−118^]{.rev}) (Figure [-@fig-normal2mci]A). However, the DMP effect sizes compared to the normal2mci group were negative (*r* = [−0.48]{.rev}, [*P* = 6.08 × 10^−24^]{.rev}; Figure [-@fig-normal2mci]A). These patterns persisted in the [participants]{.rev} who at baseline either had mild cognitive impairments (Figure [-@fig-normal2mci]B, mci2incid transition) or were cognitively normal (@suppfig-normal2incid_DMP, normal2incid transition) but later developed dementia.
We also investigated the pairwise correlations by incorporating additional CpG sites using less stringent thresholds (*P* < 1.0 × 10^−7^, threshold 7; *P* < 1.0 × 10^−6^, threshold 6; *P* < 1.0 × 10^−5^, threshold 5) [and found the same pattern]{.rev} (Figure [-@fig-normal2mci]C–D, Figures S[-@suppfig-normal2incid_extended_DMP]–S[-@suppfig-mci2incid_extended_DMP]). [Across 21 CpG selection thresholds, from all 799,149 CpG sites (no *P*-value filter) to *P* < 1.0 × 10^−10^ (95 CpG sites), every correlation kept the same sign, although the correlations were weakest when all CpG sites were included]{.rev} (Figure [-@fig-normal2mci]E–F, @suppfig-ES_corr_mci2incid_normal2mci).

The stable_mci group exhibited a distinctive methylation pattern. While the majority of the DMPs (main group, n = 343, stable_mci effect size > -0.2) showed the same correlations described above — positive with prevalent dementia (*r* = 0.68, [*P* = 1.03 × 10^−48^]{.rev}), normal2incid (*r* = 0.71, [*P* = 3.72 × 10^−53^]{.rev}) and mci2incid (*r* = 0.63, [*P* = 1.23 × 10^−39^]{.rev}), and negative with normal2mci (*r* = [−0.43]{.rev}, [*P* = 7.09 × 10^−17^]{.rev}) (@suppfig-stable_mci_DMP) — it also carried an overhanging outlier group (n = 60, stable_mci effect size < -0.2) whose effect sizes were near zero in every other group and uncorrelated with every transition (|*r*| ≤ 0.21, *P* ≥ [0.113]{.rev}; @suppfig-stable_mci_DMP). This dichotomy persisted when additional CpG sites were included at less stringent thresholds (Figures S[-@suppfig-stable_mci_extended_prev]–S[-@suppfig-stable_mci_extended_transitions]).

### [Latent dimensions differ across dementia stages]{.rev}

The preceding EWAS analysis examined individual DMP sites and did not model the underlying interdependencies among CpG sites. To capture the inherent clustering of DMP sites in relation to dementia group, we performed dimension reduction analyses using two complementary approaches, variational autoencoder (VAE) (@suppfig-vae-methodology) and UMAP, which summarize the data in different ways. VAE is a probabilistic generative model that learns a distribution over the methylation features, with each latent dimension capturing a distinct axis of variation that separates dementia groups. UMAP instead summarizes the spatial topography of the CpG data, placing [participants]{.rev} with similar epigenetic profiles close together in a low-dimensional space whose number of dimensions is set as a model parameter.

Both approaches used the same set of 403 DMP sites (*P* < 1.0 × 10^−8^; THR8) and, to capture sites of suggestive significance, the 949 CpG sites that passed the *P* < 1.0 × 10^−7^ threshold (THR7). At THR8, latent values differed most between the prevalent dementia group and the stable normal group: four of the six VAE dimensions distinguished the two (criterion of *P* < [0.01]{.rev}, t-test), with VAE_2 (*P* = 4.18 × 10^−26^), VAE_6 (*P* = 4.88 × 10^−26^) and VAE_4 (*P* = 5.82 × 10^−15^) lower and VAE_3 (*P* = 3.12 × 10^−3^) higher in prevalent dementia (Figure [-@fig-vae-boxplots]A). The stable_mci group, by contrast, was barely distinguishable from stable normal, with no VAE dimension reaching significance (Figure [-@fig-vae-boxplots]B). Both patterns held at THR7: VAE_1 (*P* = 1.44 × 10^−24^) and VAE_2 (*P* = 1.58 × 10^−17^) again separated prevalent dementia from stable normal, while stable_mci remained indistinguishable (@suppfig-vae-boxplot-t7).

We next asked whether these latent values changed progressively [along the clinical course, ordering the six groups by baseline status and subsequent trajectory (the clinical progression ordering)]{.rev}: normal2mci, stable_normal, stable_mci, normal2incid, mci2incid, and prevalent dementia. The magnitude of the latent values tracked this clinical course, decreasing near-monotonically along the ordering in VAE_6 (*P* = 5.88 × 10^−30^, ANOVA), VAE_2 (*P* = 2.02 × 10^−29^) and VAE_4 (*P* = 3.75 × 10^−17^) (Figure [-@fig-vae-boxplots]C). A monotonic gradient likewise appeared at THR7 in VAE_1 (*P* = 2.01 × 10^−27^) and VAE_2 (*P* = 2.05 × 10^−18^), the two dimensions reaching significance at that threshold (@suppfig-vae-boxplot-one-dim-t7).

UMAP recovered the same structure. Its dimensions again separated prevalent dementia from stable normal most strongly, while stable_mci stayed close to stable normal (@suppfig-umap-boxplot-t8 for THR8 and @suppfig-umap-boxplot-t7 for THR7), and selected UMAP dimensions likewise changed gradually across the progression ordering (Figure [-@fig-vae-boxplots]D for THR8; @suppfig-umap-boxplot-one-dim-t7 for THR7). A principal component analysis of the same DMP sites recovered a weaker version of this structure (data not shown).

### Latent dimension pairs reveal progression trajectory

We next examined how pairs of latent dimensions moved together across the dementia stages, using two-dimensional kernel density contours of the 403 DMP sites (*P* < 1.0 × 10^−8^; THR8) to show where [participants]{.rev} with similar epigenetic profiles clustered (VAE, Figure [-@fig-scatter-peak]A–B; UMAP, Figure [-@fig-scatter-peak]C–D). The clusters shifted gradually in latent space [along the clinical progression ordering]{.rev}: for UMAP_1 and UMAP_5, [the group contours moved]{.rev} from the lower left toward the upper right[, from]{.rev} normal2mci to prevalent dementia (Figure [-@fig-scatter-peak]C). Connecting the per-group cluster centers traced a continuous path across the stages (Figure [-@fig-scatter-peak]E–F for VAE and Figure [-@fig-scatter-peak]G–H for UMAP), and the same transition appeared across additional VAE pairs (@suppfig-vae-scatter-t8-p1) and UMAP pairs (Figures S[-@suppfig-umap-scatter-t8-p1]–S[-@suppfig-umap-scatter-t8-p2]).

We quantified this shift with the dementia progression score (DPS), which measures how closely the sequence of per-group contour centroids follows the clinical dementia ordering (see Methods; +1 if the centroids lie on a straight line in the correct order, −1 for the reversed order, and 0 for no progression). The six latent dimensions formed 15 pairs, ranked by DPS. The top VAE pairs reached DPS values of 0.442 and 0.415 (Figure [-@fig-scatter-peak]E–F) and the top UMAP pairs 0.911 and 0.834 (Figure [-@fig-scatter-peak]G–H). At THR8, permutation testing (1,000 iterations) confirmed 10 UMAP pairs and 9 VAE pairs as significant (all *P* < 0.05; Figures S[-@suppfig-vae-null-dist], S[-@suppfig-umap-null-dist] and S[-@suppfig-perm-heatmap]); at THR7 the significant UMAP pairs rose to 14 while VAE held at 9 (@suppfig-perm-heatmap).

The two methods differed for the stable_mci group: VAE placed its centroid off the progression path (Figure [-@fig-scatter-peak]E–F, @suppfig-vae-scatter-t8-p1), whereas UMAP kept it on the path (Figure [-@fig-scatter-peak]G–H, Figures S[-@suppfig-umap-scatter-t8-p1]–S[-@suppfig-umap-scatter-t8-p2]). This may reflect the VAE capturing the overhanging outlier group of stable_mci CpG sites (Figures S[-@suppfig-stable_mci_DMP]–S[-@suppfig-stable_mci_extended_transitions]).

### APOE genotype effects on DNA methylation patterns

We next asked whether these latent epigenetic patterns differed among persons with different APOE genotypes, which reflect susceptibility to Alzheimer's dementia. [APOE genotype frequencies differed across the six groups (chi-square *P* = 4.18 × 10^−13^; genotype counts by group in @supptbl-apoe-dementia).]{.rev} We grouped the six genotypes by functional role — protective (ε2/ε2, ε2/ε3), neutral (ε3/ε3), and detrimental (ε2/ε4, ε3/ε4, ε4/ε4) — following the reported per-genotype risk of Alzheimer's disease [@RN100; @RN89], and tested each latent dimension for a difference across these roles (Kruskal-Wallis test); six of the twelve dimensions differed significantly at THR8 (403 CpGs; @fig-apoe-boxplots). Two UMAP dimensions, UMAP_5 (*P* = [8.36 × 10^−4^]{.rev}) and UMAP_1 (*P* = [1.40 × 10^−3^]{.rev}), had the lowest values in protective genotypes, rose slightly in the neutral genotype, and rose further in the detrimental genotypes; UMAP_2 (*P* = [9.97 × 10^−3^]{.rev}) showed the inverse trend, higher in protective and lower in detrimental genotypes. Of three significant VAE dimensions, VAE_6 (*P* = [3.18 × 10^−3^]{.rev}) and VAE_2 (*P* = [4.23 × 10^−3^]{.rev}) decreased steadily from protective to detrimental genotypes, while VAE_4 (*P* = 0.0147) followed the same direction, albeit more weakly. At THR7 (949 CpGs), five dimensions differed by role (@suppfig-apoe-boxplot-t7): UMAP_2 was again higher in protective genotypes, whereas UMAP_1, UMAP_3, and VAE_1 increased toward the detrimental genotypes and VAE_2 differed only marginally, with overall separation weaker than at THR8.

### [Concordance with published blood EWAS of Alzheimer's disease]{.rev}

We assessed the reproducibility of effect sizes describing the association of dementia group [with methylation at individual CpG sites by comparing AGES results with two published resources covering three cohorts]{.rev}: the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) and the Australian Imaging, Biomarkers, and Lifestyle (AIBL) cohorts summarized in a meta-analysis (META) [@RN44], and the AddNeuroMed study [@RN24] (@supptbl-reference-comparison). We selected from META 96 CpG sites (*P* < 1.0 × 10^−4.5^) associated with AD (vs cognitively normal (CN) control) and compared [their effect sizes with the AGES effect sizes at the same CpG sites]{.rev}. We found moderate but significant correlations for prevalent dementia (*r* = 0.47, *P* = 7.06 × 10^−6^) and for the transition stages progressing to dementia, mci2incid (*r* = 0.52, *P* = 6.74 × 10^−7^) and normal2incid (*r* = 0.42, *P* = 7.76 × 10^−5^) (Figure [-@fig-validation]A; reference group: stable normal). Relaxing the threshold to 1.0 × 10^−4^ increased the number of CpG sites to 224, with concordance remaining robust (*r* = 0.46, 0.37, and 0.36; *P* = 5.71 × 10^−12^, [5.70]{.rev} × 10^−8^, and [1.80]{.rev} × 10^−7^ for prevalent dementia, mci2incid, and normal2incid, respectively) (Figure [-@fig-validation]A).

AddNeuroMed reported effect sizes for MCI and for AD, each relative to CN controls. Both comparisons correlated consistently with the AGES effect sizes for normal2incid, mci2incid, and prevalent dementia (*r* = 0.16 to 0.44; Figure [-@fig-validation]B). [In sign tests, more CpG sites than expected by chance had the same direction of effect in AGES and META: 54.6–68.2% for normal2incid and 55.6–71.4% for mci2incid across the six selection thresholds (one-sided binomial *P* ≤ 5.08 × 10^−4^ at each, reaching *P* = 2.12 × 10^−18^ for normal2incid and 3.74 × 10^−26^ for mci2incid at the loosest selection threshold), and 56.2–58.3% for prevalent dementia (*P* ≤ 0.0384 at all but the most stringent threshold, where *P* = 0.0778) (Figure [-@fig-validation]C). The same held for AddNeuroMed, with 61.4–67.1% concordant sites in the MCI comparison and 54.5–61.2% in the AD comparison across the three AGES groups (*P* ≤ 4.72 × 10^−3^; Figure [-@fig-validation]D).]{.rev}

### Biological pathway analysis reveals stage-specific biological processes

We conducted a pathway analysis to identify biological processes that could contribute to different stages of dementia. The number of CpG sites passing the genome-wide significance threshold was highly uneven across the five dementia groups — normal2mci (n = 5), stable_mci (n = 62), normal2incid (n = 1), mci2incid (n = 9), and prevalent dementia (n = 326) (@suppfig-pval-with-top-genes, @suppdata-DMP403) — too uneven for a balanced enrichment comparison. We therefore selected the top 1,000 CpG sites ranked by EWAS [*P* value]{.rev} for each group. Gene annotation yielded comparable numbers of associated genes: normal2mci (n = 1,474), stable_mci (n = 1,447), normal2incid (n = 1,530), mci2incid (n = 1,534), and prevalent dementia (n = 1,566) (Figure [-@fig-pathway-analysis]A[; Data S[-@suppdata-CG_normal2mci], S[-@suppdata-CG_stable_mci], S[-@suppdata-CG_normal2incid], S[-@suppdata-CG_mci2incid] and S[-@suppdata-CG_prev] list the top 2,000 CpG sites of each group, ranked by *P* value, so the top 1,000 are their first 1,000 rows]{.rev}). Despite these comparable gene counts, Gene Ontology (GO) biological process (BP) enrichment differed markedly across the groups: normal2mci yielded the most enriched GO BP terms (n = [152]{.rev}), more than three times as many as mci2incid (n = 48) and [nearly]{.rev} seven times as many as prevalent dementia (n = 22). [Most of these terms were significant in only one group: 137 of 152 (90%) in normal2mci, 9 of 12 (75%) in stable_mci, 14 of 16 (88%) in normal2incid, 30 of 48 (63%) in mci2incid, and 14 of 22 (64%) in prevalent dementia]{.rev} (Figure [-@fig-pathway-analysis]B, @suppdata-GO_top1000). [Because GO terms are nested, related terms can be enriched together, within a group as well as across groups: 32 of these 204 terms (16%) had an immediate parent or child term that was significant in another group. We therefore also counted them in a redundancy-aware way, weighting each term by the share of its immediate relatives that were not themselves significant (see Methods); the weighted numbers of terms significant in only one group were 112 in normal2mci, 7 in stable_mci, 11 in normal2incid, 26 in mci2incid, and 13 in prevalent dementia, so normal2mci still had the most.]{.rev} In the top 2,000 CpG sites, normal2mci again yielded both the most enriched GO BP terms (n = [343]{.rev}) and the most [terms significant only in that group]{.rev} (n = [195; weighted count 143]{.rev}; @suppfig-upset-top2000, @suppdata-GO_top2000).

We then grouped the [GO BP terms significant in only one group]{.rev} into functional categories[, counting each term by its weight (Figure [-@fig-pathway-analysis]C shows the weighted counts)]{.rev} (Tables S[-@supptbl-top1000-normal2mci], S[-@supptbl-top1000-stable-mci], S[-@supptbl-top1000-normal2incid], S[-@supptbl-top1000-mci2incid] and S[-@supptbl-top1000-prev]; [below, each category is followed by its number of BP terms and their weighted count]{.rev}). The normal2mci transition was enriched for ion transport and regulation ([13; 10]{.rev}), synaptic function and organization ([8; 6]{.rev}), [extracellular matrix organization (7; 6), and immune response (7; 5)]{.rev}. The stable_mci group was enriched for hypoxia response ([3; 2]{.rev}), the normal2incid transition for synaptic vesicle control ([4; 3]{.rev}), the mci2incid transition for hormone signaling ([5; 4]{.rev}) and cell migration and organization ([7; 6]{.rev}), and prevalent dementia for cell-cycle regulation ([3; 2]{.rev}). [No term in these categories had an immediate GO parent or child term that was significant in another group, except one of the seven mci2incid cell migration and organization terms (@suppdata-GO_top1000).]{.rev} The normal2incid and mci2incid transitions shared two functional categories, both related to neurodevelopmental processes: development and differentiation, and neural development and regulation. [With the top 2,000 CpG sites, each of these categories was again enriched in the same group, but not all remained specific to it; for example, cell-cycle regulation was also enriched in stable_mci (@suppfig-barplot-top2000). These processes were inferred from whole blood, so they describe genes near blood methylation differences; such differences may relate to dementia through systemic routes, for example immune or vascular processes, rather than by reflecting changes in the brain.]{.rev}
